subject: arts-music
lesson_title: Synthesis and review: symbol and visual metaphor
essential_question: How can understanding visual storytelling and composition help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Connect symbol and visual metaphor to the unit’s other ideas and select evidence that shows readiness for assessment.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of symbol and visual metaphor.
Check, revise, or improve work about symbol and visual metaphor using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about symbol and visual metaphor.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool

Household-accessible route: pencil or pen and scrap paper are enough. For sound or performance work, tap, clap, use spoken syllables, move a finger, or notate silently. Specialized art materials, instruments, paid software, cameras, microphones, and recording devices are optional and never affect credit.
task_brief: Day 10 of "Visual Storytelling and Composition" (unit 1, grade 7) is a synthesis on symbol and visual metaphor. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 40–60 minutes. The unit is working toward: Create a visual narrative or series with a process journal and artist statement. Today's work contributes to that by handling symbol and visual metaphor at the synthesis and review stage, against the unit's wider topics of composition and focal point, value color and mood, perspective and depth, and symbol and visual metaphor. This session produces reviewable evidence toward the unit performance task.
primary_task: Draw symbol and visual metaphor together with the other ideas built across this unit, including value color and mood. Produce a single organised artifact — an annotated portfolio page, a comparison chart, or a mapped set of your own studies — showing how at least three of the unit's ideas relate and where each one shows up in work you actually made. Then make or analyse one short example that needs two of them at once and label which is doing what. Name the idea you are least confident about and what would settle it. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about symbol and visual metaphor, and it belongs to "Visual Storytelling and Composition", which also covers separate topics such as composition and focal point. Close out with this check before you stop: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about symbol and visual metaphor; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. At grade 7 the bar is independent work with reasoning that a reader can follow without you present, plus one stated check you ran on your own result before submitting.
requirements: Meet this lesson's own success criteria: The learner completes the central task about symbol and visual metaphor., The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer., and The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
Address the lesson objective: Connect symbol and visual metaphor to the unit’s other ideas and select evidence that shows readiness for assessment.
Produce the deliverable for a synthesis: One organised artifact relating at least three unit ideas to work actually made, plus a two-idea example with each part labelled.
Show the process, not only the result — a working log, draft, or annotated study.
Complete the critique criteria list in this package before submitting.
deliverable: One organised artifact relating at least three unit ideas to work actually made, plus a two-idea example with each part labelled.
critique_criteria: At least three unit ideas are related in one organised artifact, each located in work the student actually made.
One short example genuinely requires two ideas at once, with each labelled.
The least-confident idea is named along with what would settle it.
All included work is the student's own or properly cited.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This work spans sessions, so supply a written milestone plan, explicit checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown. Executive-function load — sequencing, holding the plan in mind, remembering where the work stopped — must not become a silent part of what is being assessed.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting symbol and visual metaphor.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for symbol and visual metaphor follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for symbol and visual metaphor, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for symbol and visual metaphor works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of symbol and visual metaphor, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking symbol and visual metaphor mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply symbol and visual metaphor under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on symbol and visual metaphor rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
